title: 3.7L Engine Controls: Component Locations
introduction:
I use these drawings as an engine-control address book: find the highlighted part, follow its callout, then read the matching description in that drawing’s table. Start with the front view, move to the rear view, and use the vehicle-body view to locate the control module.

These locations apply to the 3.7L Duratec. Keep RH/LH and intake/exhaust labels attached to the component names; screen position alone is a poor guide when the drawing changes viewpoints. The illustrations expose components for identification, so they do not establish installed access, connector release methods, electrical tests or removal steps.

edits.why: I orient this view by the large throttle-body opening in the foreground and the curved intake runners behind it. Follow the blue highlights to the adjacent table, taking care to distinguish RH from LH and intake from exhaust. VCT means variable camshaft timing: the oil control solenoids help adjust valve timing. MAPT means manifold absolute pressure and temperature. Similar-looking connectors are neighbors, not interchangeable addresses.

The large toothed ring anchors the rear-engine viewpoint; the exhaust pipes extend down either side. Trace each leader to its highlighted component rather than assuming nearby connectors serve the same job. CKP means crankshaft position, KS means knock sensor, and CHT reports cylinder-head temperature. Keep the CMP intake/exhaust distinctions and the separate HO2S and catalyst-monitor labels intact. This view also shows components between the cylinder banks, without teaching how to uncover them.

I use the transparent body view to place the blue module beside the strut tower and inner body panel. The PCM uses sensor information and stored strategies to manage engine and powertrain functions, including commands to controlled devices. Finding its location is useful orientation; a fault code involving a controlled component does not by itself prove the PCM needs replacement.
